title: Logistic regression vs. t-test: assumptions and applications

cues.en: In the previous video I taught you about logistic regression, and in earlier videos we have used t tests.
cues.zh: 上一支影片介紹了邏輯斯迴歸，更早的影片也使用過 t 檢定。

cues.en: So what is the difference between a logistic regression and a t test?
cues.zh: 那麼，邏輯斯迴歸與 t 檢定有何不同？

cues.en: And when would you use which method?
cues.zh: 什麼時候該用哪一種方法？

cues.en: That is the goal of this video.
cues.zh: 這就是這支影片的目標。

cues.en: And I'll start with some discussions and then switch to a code demo where you can see how these two analyses relate to each other in simulated data.
cues.zh: 我會先討論一些概念，接著切換到程式示範，讓你從模擬資料看出這兩種分析的關係。

cues.en: I'll start with showing the equations for these two analyses.
cues.zh: 首先，來看這兩種分析的方程式。

cues.en: I hope that both of these equations look familiar to you from the previous video, and from elsewhere in this course or another statistics or machine learning course.
cues.zh: 希望你看過上一支影片，以及這門課的其他部分，或其他統計與機器學習課程後，會對這兩個方程式感到熟悉。

cues.en: The goal of a logistic regression is to develop a mathematical equation that generates a probability
cues.zh: 邏輯斯迴歸的目標，是建立一個數學方程式，產生

cues.en: that each data sample belongs to one of two categories.
cues.zh: 每筆資料樣本屬於兩個類別之一的機率。

cues.en: On the other hand, a T test is a measure of the normalized difference between two means of two data samples, and that is normalized by their standard errors.
cues.zh: 另一方面，t 檢定衡量的是兩組資料平均數之間，經標準誤正規化後的差異。

cues.en: So let's imagine a scenario where we are measuring the activations of a neuron somewhere in an LM for
cues.zh: 假設有這樣的情境：我們測量語言模型中某處的一個神經元，

cues.en: two different categories of words, let's say nouns and verbs.
cues.zh: 對兩種不同類別的詞，例如名詞與動詞，所產生的活化。

cues.en: We could use a logistic regression to predict the probability that each token is a noun based on the activation of that neuron.
cues.zh: 我們可以用邏輯斯迴歸，根據該神經元的活化，預測每個 token 是名詞的機率。

cues.en: And we could do a t test to see if there is a significant difference in the activation between nouns and verbs.
cues.zh: 也可以做 t 檢定，查看名詞與動詞的活化是否有顯著差異。

cues.en: So in this example, you can actually use both analyses on exactly the same data.
cues.zh: 所以在這個例子中，同一份資料其實可以做這兩種分析。

cues.en: Both analyses are perfectly reasonable and valid and appropriate statistical measures.
cues.zh: 兩者都是完全合理、有效且適用的統計測量。

cues.en: So when should you use which one and what's the difference between them?
cues.zh: 那該在什麼時候用哪一個？它們又有什麼不同？

cues.en: So I have organized their differences into this table here where you will see the discussion points and how they are related for the two different analyses.
cues.zh: 我把差異整理成這張表，列出討論重點，以及它們在兩種分析中的關係。

cues.en: Let's begin with the key assumptions.
cues.zh: 先從主要假設開始。

cues.en: For a logistic regression, we assume that the data are drawn from one population, that is, all of the sampled data.
cues.zh: 對邏輯斯迴歸，我們假設資料來自同一個母體，也就是所有抽樣資料，

cues.en: For example, all the neurons or all the tokens have the same characteristics, but the rate of belonging to one category.
cues.zh: 例如所有神經元或所有 token，都具有相同特徵，但屬於某一類別的比例，

cues.en: For example, nouns versus verbs varies according to activation value.
cues.zh: 例如名詞相對於動詞，會隨活化值而變動。

cues.en: In contrast, the t test makes the assumption that the two groups are drawn from distinct populations.
cues.zh: 相對地，t 檢定假設兩組資料來自不同的母體。

cues.en: In other words, for a t test, we are evaluating whether nouns and verbs are actually really distinct from each other.
cues.zh: 換句話說，做 t 檢定時，我們評估名詞與動詞是否真的彼此不同。

cues.en: Whereas with logistic regression, we're testing whether the probability of a particular activation value is associated with nouns versus verbs.
cues.zh: 而做邏輯斯迴歸時，則是在檢驗某個活化值的機率，是否與名詞或動詞有關。

cues.en: So the t test also has an additional assumption that the data are normally distributed.
cues.zh: t 檢定還有一項額外假設，就是資料呈常態分布。

cues.en: And that is not an assumption that we require for logistic regression.
cues.zh: 邏輯斯迴歸則不需要這個假設。

cues.en: In terms of the outcome of the analysis, the logistic regression gives us a parameter, or maybe a
cues.zh: 就分析結果而言，邏輯斯迴歸會提供一個參數，或是一組

cues.en: set of parameters that we can use to generate a predictive statistical model of the data.
cues.zh: 參數，讓我們建立資料的預測統計模型。

cues.en: In contrast, the t test is actually not give us a parameter.
cues.zh: 相對地，t 檢定並不提供參數，

cues.en: Instead, it provides the t statistic, which is a measure of effect size.
cues.zh: 而是提供 t 統計量，也就是一種效果量指標。

cues.en: And this relates to the key distinction in application, which is that a logistic regression can be used to generate a prediction.
cues.zh: 這也連結到應用上的關鍵區別：邏輯斯迴歸能用來產生預測，

cues.en: So generate a probability that each data sample belongs to each category.
cues.zh: 也就是產生每筆資料樣本屬於各類別的機率。

cues.en: And in contrast, the t test is not used to generate predictions, certainly not at the level of an individual data sample.
cues.zh: 相對地，t 檢定並非用來產生預測，尤其不是預測個別資料樣本。

cues.en: So to make this more concrete, if you have activation values from a neuron, then a logistic regression
cues.zh: 說得具體一點，如果有某個神經元的活化值，邏輯斯迴歸

cues.en: can help you generate a prediction about whether that token that elicited the activation was a noun or a verb.
cues.zh: 可以協助預測引發這次活化的 token，是名詞還是動詞。

cues.en: But that kind of predictive model is not what a t test is designed for.
cues.zh: 但這種預測模型並不是 t 檢定的設計用途。

cues.en: Another difference is that logistic regression is easy to extend to multiple variables.
cues.zh: 另一項差異是，邏輯斯迴歸很容易擴充到多個變數。

cues.en: So not just the activation from one neuron.
cues.zh: 不只使用單一神經元的活化，

cues.en: But let's say you want to look at the activations of an ensemble of neurons to see whether the relationships
cues.zh: 例如你也許想查看一群神經元的活化，研究各個神經元之間的

cues.en: of the activations across the neurons can predict whether a token is a noun or a verb.
cues.zh: 活化關係，能否預測一個 token 是名詞還是動詞。

cues.en: In contrast, the t test is only designed for one dependent variable and two groups.
cues.zh: 相對地，t 檢定只針對一個依變數與兩個群組設計。

cues.en: Of course, there are statistical analyses for more than two samples, but that would be, for example, an Anova or a linear regression and not a t test.
cues.zh: 當然，也有處理超過兩組樣本的統計分析，例如變異數分析或線性迴歸，但那就不是 t 檢定。

cues.en: So taken together, all this stuff in consideration, you would use a logistic regression when you want
cues.zh: 所以，綜合考量以上各點，當你想

cues.en: to make predictions about a category or token label, or when you want to extend the analysis to using multiple variables to predict a category label.
cues.zh: 預測類別或 token 標籤，或是想將分析擴充為利用多個變數預測類別標籤時，就會使用邏輯斯迴歸。

cues.en: And you would use a t test to determine whether there are significant differences between two token types in a neuron.
cues.zh: 若要判斷某個神經元對兩種 token 類型的反應有沒有顯著差異，則會使用 t 檢定。

cues.en: Now, of course, the t test is also fairly versatile.
cues.zh: 當然，t 檢定的用途也相當靈活。

cues.en: You can run a t test for different tokens in each neuron in a particular layer, and you can also use
cues.zh: 你可以對特定層中的每個神經元，針對不同 token 進行 t 檢定，也能用

cues.en: a t test for comparing the overall activations for different token types between different layers or
cues.zh: t 檢定比較不同 token 類型，在不同層或

cues.en: different groups of neurons, for example, different attention heads inside a transformer.
cues.zh: 不同神經元群組中的整體活化，例如 Transformer 內不同的注意力頭。

cues.en: Now, that is not something you could do with a logistic regression.
cues.zh: 這就不是邏輯斯迴歸能做的事情。

cues.en: And I would also like to stress that my goal in this slide was to highlight the differences between these two analyses.
cues.zh: 我也想強調，這張投影片的目的是凸顯兩種分析的差異。

cues.en: They also have a lot in common.
cues.zh: 它們同樣有很多共通點。

cues.en: And that is what I want to focus on in the Python demo.
cues.zh: 這就是 Python 示範要著重的部分。

cues.zh: 這是很好的實驗方式，因為使用的資料完全相同，分析則略有不同。

cues.zh: 左邊這張圖的 x 軸是邏輯斯迴歸的 beta 值，y 軸是 t 值。

cues.en: Each little green circle here shows a different simulation with a different effect size between the nouns and the verbs.
cues.zh: 每個綠色小圓點，代表一次名詞與動詞間具有不同效果量的模擬。

cues.en: Now the regression and the t tests do not give identical results for a variety of reasons, but they are really, really similar.
cues.zh: 由於各種原因，迴歸與 t 檢定的結果並不完全相同，但確實非常相似。

cues.en: And you see more divergences as you get to extreme values.
cues.zh: 越接近極端值，分歧就越大。

cues.en: And I'll discuss a little bit more why this happens when we switch to code.

cues.en: And here on the right you see the negative log of the p values for the logistic regression and the t test.
cues.zh: 右邊則是邏輯斯迴歸與 t 檢定之 P 值的負對數。

cues.en: The dashed lines here correspond to a statistical significance threshold of 0.05.
cues.zh: 虛線對應 0.05 的統計顯著性門檻。

cues.zh: 也就是邏輯斯迴歸與 t 檢定，在這裡這些點上都不顯著。

cues.en: And when the results are statistically significant they are significant in both tests.
cues.zh: 而結果達到統計顯著時，兩種檢定也都顯著。

cues.zh: 但記得，它們不是同一個東西。

cues.en: They come from different analyses, different formulas, different math, different statistical approaches, different estimation procedures.
cues.zh: 它們來自不同的分析、不同的公式、不同的數學、不同的統計方法與不同的估計程序。

cues.en: There's a lot of differences between logistic regression and a t statistic.
cues.zh: 邏輯斯迴歸與 t 統計量有很多差異。

cues.en: But in this kind of a situation where you have two labels and continuous data like neuron activation levels, you can use them in the same way.
cues.zh: 但在這種情況下，也就是有兩種標籤，以及神經元活化程度這類連續資料時，可以用它們做相同的事情。

cues.en: They will basically give not exactly the same results, but really, really strongly comparable results, at least until you get out to some extreme values.
cues.zh: 結果不會完全相同，但確實非常具有可比性，至少在碰到某些極端值之前如此。

cues.en: And basically what happens is that the estimation of the logistic regression becomes increasingly difficult
cues.zh: 基本上，當兩個類別完全分離時，邏輯斯迴歸的估計會越來越困難，

cues.en: and numerically unstable when you get perfect separation between the two categories.
cues.zh: 而且會出現數值不穩定。

cues.en: We can actually demonstrate that by setting this out to let's say six.
cues.zh: 我們可以把這裡設定為，例如 6，來示範。

cues.en: How about minus six to plus six?
cues.zh: 改成 −6 到 +6 如何？

cues.en: So what's happening here is that these means are going to be so far apart from each other.
cues.zh: 這時的情況是，這些平均數彼此會相距非常遠。

cues.en: The means for the nouns and the verbs at these extremes, that the logistic regression is actually going to run into some trouble.
cues.zh: 在兩端的極端情況下，名詞與動詞的平均數相距太遠，邏輯斯迴歸就會遇到麻煩。

cues.en: You will see we in fact got some error messages and a bunch of warnings.
cues.zh: 可以看到，確實出現了一些錯誤訊息，以及許多警告。

cues.en: Perfect separation.
cues.zh: 完全分離。

cues.en: This seems like it should be a good thing that you have perfect separability, but you end up with just numerical issues because of the classification.
cues.zh: 具有完全可分性，聽起來應該是好事，但分類時會遇到數值問題。

cues.en: Okay, so we still get some warning messages, but no errors.
cues.zh: 好，現在仍有一些警告，但沒有錯誤。

cues.en: And now you can see that the beta values and the t statistics do correspond to each other very well.
cues.zh: 可以看到，beta 值與 t 統計量仍然對應得很好，

cues.en: Until you get to these extreme values where the data are just too good and the nonlinear estimation techniques are just not working very well.
cues.zh: 直到這些極端值，因為資料分得太好了，非線性估計技術就無法好好運作。

cues.en: Okay, but let me go back to some more normal ranges here.
cues.zh: 不過，先回到比較正常的範圍。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So here again.
cues.zh: 這裡再看一次。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So now you see the statistical significance is these are the p values.
cues.zh: 現在可以看到統計顯著性，這些是 P 值。

cues.en: You can ignore these lines here.
cues.zh: 先忽略這幾條線。

cues.en: Actually we can just change those.
cues.zh: 其實可以直接修改它們，

cues.en: So that is just set that to be plotting lines at 0.05 instead of the minus log of 0.05.
cues.zh: 讓它們畫在 0.05，而不是 0.05 的負對數。

cues.en: Now this is fine.
cues.zh: 這樣也可以，

cues.en: There's nothing wrong with showing data like this, but all of the p values are kind of scrunched up here close to zero.
cues.zh: 這種畫法沒有錯，但所有 P 值幾乎都擠在接近零的地方。

cues.en: And you just don't really get an appreciation of the full range of the distribution of p values.
cues.zh: 你不太能看出 P 值分布的完整範圍。

cues.en: So that is why I am using of minus the log.
cues.zh: 所以我才使用負對數。

cues.en: So now I'm going to put all of this back and you will see the difference.
cues.zh: 現在把這些設定都改回去，就能看出差異。

cues.en: So minus log.
cues.zh: 取負對數。

cues.en: There you go.
cues.zh: 這樣好了。

cues.en: Rerun that code.
cues.zh: 重新執行這段程式。

cues.en: Rerun that code.
cues.zh: 重新執行這段程式。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 對。

cues.en: And I think now it's just a little bit visually clear what is going on here.
cues.zh: 我覺得現在比較容易從圖上看懂發生了什麼事。

cues.en: Again when you get to some extreme values then things start getting a little bit wonky from the regression, but that's not really a problem.
cues.zh: 同樣地，到了某些極端值，迴歸就會開始變得有點怪，但問題不大。

cues.en: You still see that when one test is non-significant, the other test is non-significant.
cues.zh: 仍然可以看到，一種檢定不顯著時，另一種檢定也不顯著；

cues.en: When one test is significant, the other test is significant.
cues.zh: 一種檢定顯著時，另一種檢定也顯著。

cues.en: So there's a lot of consistency between these two measures.
cues.zh: 所以這兩個指標具有很高的一致性。

cues.en: One thing, just as a reminder, when you're looking at minus the log of p, then you want to look for large values.
cues.zh: 提醒一下，看 P 值的負對數時，要找的是大數值。

cues.en: This means a small p value corresponds to a large minus the log of the p value.
cues.zh: 也就是說，小 P 值會對應到大的負對數 P 值。

cues.en: There's one more thing I wanted to mention, just FYI here about logistic regression.
cues.zh: 關於邏輯斯迴歸，還想順便補充一點，

cues.en: Uh, and that is the order in which you present the labels.
cues.zh: 就是標籤輸入的順序。

cues.en: So let's say, for example, that I would swap the verbs and the nouns.
cues.zh: 例如，假設將動詞與名詞互換。

cues.en: So now I'm entering the data into the logistic regression first as the nouns and then as the verbs.
cues.zh: 現在輸入邏輯斯迴歸的資料，會先是名詞，接著才是動詞。

cues.en: And basically what that means is that previously I was associating verbs with zero and nouns with one.
cues.zh: 基本上，原本我是將動詞設為 0、名詞設為 1，

cues.en: And now I'm associating nouns with zero and verbs with one.
cues.zh: 現在則將名詞設為 0、動詞設為 1。

cues.en: And what does that do?
cues.zh: 這會造成什麼影響？

cues.en: The short answer is that it does nothing except flip the sign of the beta value.
cues.zh: 簡單來說，除了將 beta 值的正負號反轉以外，沒有任何影響。

cues.en: So now you see the same kind of relationship, the same strength of the relationship between the logistic regression beta and the t test t value.
cues.zh: 可以看到，邏輯斯迴歸 beta 與 t 檢定 t 值之間，仍是同樣類型、同樣強度的關係，

cues.en: But now it's negative.
cues.zh: 但現在是負相關。

cues.en: And what if we want to make that positive.
cues.zh: 若想讓它變成正相關呢？

cues.en: No problem whatsoever.
cues.zh: 完全沒問題。

cues.en: We can also swap the order of the t test.
cues.zh: 也可以把 t 檢定的順序互換。

cues.en: Again when you swap the order in a t test you're not actually changing the statistics.
cues.zh: 同樣地，將 t 檢定的順序互換，實際上不會改變統計結果。

cues.en: You're only changing.
cues.zh: 只會改變……

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: Let me just run into some numerical issues again.
cues.zh: 這裡又遇到一些數值問題了。

cues.en: You're not changing anything in the statistics or the statistical significance.
cues.zh: 你並沒有改變統計結果或統計顯著性，

cues.en: The only thing that you're doing is flipping the sign of the numerator.
cues.zh: 唯一做的事情，就是反轉分子的正負號。

cues.en: So the t value goes from being negative to positive because you're subtracting the means the other way.
cues.zh: 因此 t 值從負變正，因為平均數相減的方向反過來了。

cues.en: Okay, that was just a little point.
cues.zh: 好，這只是個小補充。

cues.en: The very last thing I want to mention is the relationship between a one sample t test and a paired sample t test.
cues.zh: 最後還想說明單一樣本 t 檢定與成對樣本 t 檢定的關係。

cues.en: So the code looks different.
cues.zh: 程式碼看起來不同，

cues.en: The functions are different.
cues.zh: 使用的函式也不同。

cues.en: T test one sample for one sample t test rel for related samples.
cues.zh: 單一樣本 t 檢定使用 ttest_1samp，相關樣本則使用 ttest_rel，

cues.en: Or most people call it paired samples.
cues.zh: 也就是大多數人所稱的成對樣本。

cues.en: Here I'm providing two inputs for the paired samples t test.
cues.zh: 這裡提供兩個輸入，進行成對樣本 t 檢定；

cues.en: Here I'm providing one input for the data.
cues.zh: 這裡則提供一個資料輸入，

cues.en: And that is the difference between these two activation values.
cues.zh: 也就是這兩組活化值的差。

cues.en: And then zero is the null hypothesis that we are going to test against and forget about what the numbers are.
cues.zh: 0 則是要拿來比較的虛無假設。先別管這些數值是多少，

cues.en: That doesn't matter.
cues.zh: 那不重要。

cues.en: The important thing here is that these numbers are exactly the same as these numbers.
cues.zh: 這裡重要的是，這些數值與那些數值完全相同。

cues.en: In other words, a paired samples t test is mathematically equivalent to a one sample t test on the
cues.zh: 換句話說，成對樣本 t 檢定，在數學上等同於對

cues.en: differences between the data values for the two different samples.
cues.zh: 兩組不同樣本之資料值的差，進行單一樣本 t 檢定。

cues.en: That is not the case for a two samples t test.
cues.zh: 雙樣本 t 檢定就不是這樣。

cues.en: It is the case for a one sample t test versus a paired samples t test.
cues.zh: 這種關係存在於單一樣本 t 檢定與成對樣本 t 檢定之間。
